title: Initiative Dependency Beacon: Lightweight Contracting & Failure Containment
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When multiple initiatives across Eng, Design, Security, and Infra overlap there is inconsistent visibility into which integration points are contractually required for a release, and insufficient signal when a partner scope slips. This causes last-minute scope cuts and unreliable rollouts.

Goal: Create a lightweight, low-friction dependency "beacon" pattern and a short escalation contract that teams attach to initiative cards. The beacon must provide: (1) minimal required interface expectations (inputs/outputs/deadlines), (2) explicit risk posture and fallback options, (3) a small telemetry pulse that surfaces health and readiness into the Console/PM dashboards, and (4) an automated escalation path for missed commitments.

Scope: Pilot across 6 initiatives in Q2 that represent a mix of Hosted API features, Dedicated capacity changes, and Console UX work. Deliverables span docs, a dependency schema template, a minimal telemetry spike (availability/readiness), and an ops runbook for negotiated rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable 'Dependency Beacon' template exists in Confluence and is linked from initiative cards
Teams can attach a beacon to an initiative in the PM intake within 10 minutes
Telemetry pulse (readiness boolean + last-updated timestamp) for attached beacons appears in the Roadmap Signals dashboard with <=5m ingestion latency
At least 4 partner teams (Eng/Design/Security/Infra) sign the lightweight escalation contract for pilot initiatives
One simulated miss is executed in staging to validate automated escalation and fallback behavior documented in the runbook
deliverables: Template fields: owner, required API surfaces, DWG (deliver-by) dates, fallback behavior, SLO-equivalent readiness gate
Roadmap Signals dashboard tile showing 'beacon readiness' for pilot initiatives
Minimal ingestion pipeline (event webhook -> ingestion -> dashboard) with schema and transformation rules
Ops runbook: escalation steps, who-to-call matrix, rollback checklist, communications template
risks: Low adoption risk if template is perceived as heavy; mitigated by 1-page template and onboarding session
Telemetry work may surface new infra quotas; scope to a small heartbeat event to reduce cost
Stakeholder resistance from teams that prefer ad-hoc communication; mitigated via exec sponsorship and pilot feedback loop
Cross-team alignment on what constitutes 'readiness' could vary — will ship minimal boolean first and iterate
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize template and escalate contract language with Legal/Trust (light review only)
Week 2: Instrument heartbeat event for pilot integrations (internal webhook schema v1)
Week 3: Create Roadmap Signals dashboard and add pilot initiatives
Week 4: Run simulated missed-dependency in staging and validate escalation path
Week 5: Retro, incorporate feedback, and expand to +10 initiatives for next cycle
metrics_and_signals: Beacon attached: count of initiatives with a beacon (target 6 in pilot)
Readiness rate: percent of attached beacons reporting ready=true
Escalation count: number of automated escalations triggered
Mean time from missed heartbeat to ack by owning team
Reduction in last-minute scope changes for pilot initiatives (qualitative post-mortem)
